topics.flagship-ru-ua: Envoys from Kyiv, Moscow and Washington held a fresh round of talks, their first meeting since February, covering security guarantees, territorial concessions and a Europe-wide security framework, while Trump insists peace is close. Lavrov said Russia cannot agree to an immediate ceasefire without knowing what comes next, and wants the future European security architecture discussed first. Separately, two industry sources say Ukrainian drone strikes since late October have cut Russian oil refining capacity by about 30%, and Ukrainian intelligence reportedly examined a nearly intact K5-K cruise-missile variant of the Geran-5 drone.
topics.flagship-ir-il: France summoned Iran's ambassador over alleged cyber 'sabotage' of supermarket refrigeration and says it is seeking tough sanctions to deter further cyberattacks across Europe. A Republican lawmaker brought eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth, accusing him of waging unlawful wars on Iran and Venezuela. In Gaza, a woman and three children were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in heavy rain. Other items include Canada reimposing sanctions on 11 Iranian entities, a report that Iran lifted its 2,000km missile range limit, and a US indictment of three men over alleged terror plots including one against a UK air base.
topics.T15: Chile's Valparaíso region ran a tsunami drill on 5 November with 328,329 participants, with all establishments reaching safe zones within 27 minutes. Flooding in Florida closed a 90-bed rehabilitation hospital in Melbourne and closed DeSoto County parks. In British Columbia, Zeballos evacuation orders after a landslide are expected to last through Friday as more heavy rain is forecast.
topics.T01: Myanmar's military says it seized a key resistance command headquarters and 10 other bases in the south. Pakistan's deputy PM said the Makkah defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye is not aimed at any country. Houthi sniper fire and shelling reportedly wounded five civilians in Taiz.
topics.T02: Coverage is sparse and mostly generic, covering malnutrition, school hunger in South Africa, and El Niño risks to Myanmar and Nigeria. A small study of 206 women in Gaza links war hardships to adverse maternal health outcomes, including malnutrition.
topics.T04: A DG ECHO map dated 10 November tracks an Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak and EU response across the DRC, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda, though the item offers no case details. Other items are largely background on anthrax and noma, plus a report on scabies in Israeli prisons.
topics.T05: Trump renewed the national emergency declaration over Nicaragua on November 3. Japan is reportedly watching for shifts in Trump's foreign policy after his midterm setback, and a South Korean spy agency view casts Kim Ju Ae as likely heir. Other items are domestic political stories from India, Nigeria and Sri Lanka, with limited sourcing.
topics.T06: A report cited in coverage says Russia-linked and other networks spread false claims during riots in France, including an EU-highlighted Russian effort fabricating migrant-violence stories. Another outlet describes France as on edge amid riots as Rubio met G7 leaders in Paris. A separate study tracks seasonal patterns in Kenyan farmer protests.
topics.T08: At least 10 police were reportedly killed in a militant attack on a convoy in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and a separate checkpost attack in Hangu killed one policeman with three missing. A Hull man is on trial over an alleged plot to petrol-bomb a hotel and kill migrants, and a Montreal Jewish school shooter was sentenced to 66 months. Reported Nigeria attacks in Benue and Plateau continue.
topics.T10: Democrats who won Congress may use the NDAA and the Dec. 11 funding deadline to hold defense spending near $1 trillion, making Trump's $1.5T request unlikely. The UK carrier HMS Prince of Wales is reportedly using small drones for missions once done by helicopters. Romania could receive about 1.2 billion euros through the EU SAFE instrument by year-end.
topics.T11: The UK- and France-led Coalition of the Willing launched its first military exercise in Poland, which analysts say highlights Europe's proposed Ukraine troop deployment conflicting with Russia's position. India and Oman began the Naseem Al Bahr naval exercise, a 7,000-troop US exercise is under way in Hawaii through Nov. 17, and the IDF is drilling in the Galilee and Be'er Sheva areas. An analysis also examines a PLA 'silent' exercise on dispersing naval forces into the Western Pacific.
topics.T12: Vanderbilt University suffered a ransomware attack, with the group claiming extensive data theft and most systems still restricted. Commentary on the French supermarket incident asks how everyday infrastructure became part of the battlefield, and an Irish conference warned Ireland is underprepared for cyber and hybrid threats. See also the France-Iran summons under Iran / Israel / Middle East.
topics.T13: Coverage is scattered: an ICE subpoena concerning the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC, a lawsuit by a drone company against the UK Home Office over Channel surveillance, and Spanish VOX leader Abascal calling for remigration. No single dominant story emerges.
topics.T16: California voters rejected a ballot measure to tax billionaires' wealth. In Israel, parliament was sworn in amid coalition deadlock with Gadi Eisenkot tasked to form a government, and Shin Bet found no evidence of foreign interference in the election. Other items cover US midterm aftermath, New Zealand coalition talks, and the UN Security Council briefing on South Sudan's elections scheduled for 22 December.

bluf: Envoys from Ukraine, Russia and the US held a new round of talks, their first since February, covering security guarantees, territorial concessions and a European security framework, with Trump insisting peace is close. Lavrov said Russia will not accept an immediate ceasefire before the future security architecture is discussed. France summoned Iran's ambassador over alleged sabotage of supermarket refrigeration systems and says it is seeking tough sanctions to deter further cyberattacks across Europe. A Republican lawmaker filed eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth, accusing him of waging unlawful wars on Iran and Venezuela. In Gaza, a woman and three small children were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in torrential rain, underscoring the risks to displaced Palestinians this winter. Formula 1 confirmed the 2026 season will end with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix as planned, with Imola stood down as a backup. Separately, industry sources say Ukrainian drone strikes since late October have cut Russian oil refining capacity by about 30%. The UK- and France-led Coalition of the Willing also began its first exercise in Poland, which analysts say sits uneasily with Russia's stance on security arrangements.
